groups.title: Simulate SRTF and derive waiting or turnaround time
groups.subject: 08-operating-systems
groups.rationale: Each question supplies process arrival times and one CPU burst per process, requires simulating preemptive shortest remaining time first (called SRPT in 2004), and derives an average from process completion times. They share the scheduling procedure, not identical statements or answers: 2004 and 2025 ask average turnaround with different inputs and preemption sequences; 2024 asks average waiting and additionally compares a nonpreemptive SJF schedule. Keep every variant accessible. Exclude conceptual scheduling properties, policy identification without an arrival/burst simulation, and CPU/I/O idle-time or utilization problems requiring alternating I/O phases. Sharing the CPU-scheduling topic alone is insufficient. The 2014 set 3 and 2017 set 1 variants each ask average SRTF waiting time from four-process tables; their changed inputs form a reviewed numbers-repeat pair within this broader pattern.

groups.title: Solve fixed-ratio recurrences by comparing the nonrecursive cost
groups.subject: 05-algorithms
groups.rationale: Each requires extracting a,b and the nonrecursive cost in T(n)=aT(n/b)+f(n), comparing f with n^(log_b a), and obtaining the asymptotic order. The values and dominating cases differ. The 2026 variant repeats this procedure twice because T2 supplies the cost in T1. Exclude square-root argument substitutions, unequal splits, unit decrements, symbolic theorem-validity statements and mixed-form recurrence option sets; this is not all recurrence questions.

sources.notes: Full source page inspected, including four choices. T(1)=1; T(n)=2T(floor(n/2))+sqrt(n) for n>=2. Compare the nonrecursive cost against n^(log_2 2) to select the linear upper bound. Explicit floor is retained. No figure or shared premise.

Full archive page inspected, including four choices. T(n)=n for n<=3, otherwise T(n/3)+cn, with positive constant c. Fixed-ratio recurrence with linear nonrecursive cost; compare against n^(log_3 1), then select tight order. No figure or shared context.
Full archive page inspected. Printed Q13 gives T(n)=2T(n/2)+log n and T(1)=1, with four asymptotic choices. Compare logarithmic toll against n^(log_2 2). No figure or shared context.

Full source page and all four options inspected. For n>1, T1(n)=4T1(n/2)+T2(n), T2(n)=5T2(n/4)+Theta(log_2 n); both base values are 1 for n<=1. First solve T2 using the fixed-ratio comparison, then use its order as the toll in T1 and apply the same comparison again. This sequential two-recurrence dependency is an additional step, not an identical question. No diagram or external context.

groups.title: Unroll a doubling recurrence with a unit decrement
groups.subject: 05-algorithms
groups.rationale: Both produce or state T(n)=2T(n-1)+g(n). Unroll the recurrence (equivalently normalize by 2^n) and sum weighted nonrecursive costs. The 2004 code requires deriving this cost recurrence and has constant work per call; the 2025 explicit n*2^n cost changes the summation and introduces a polynomial factor. These are procedure variants, not repeats; do not use the fixed-ratio Master theorem for either.

sources.notes: Full source pages 11 and 12 inspected to cover the stem, code and all choices. The positive-input recursive C function returns 1 at n=1, otherwise calls recursive(n-1) twice and adds their results. Ordinary nonmemoized call-tree cost gives T(n)=2T(n-1)+Theta(1). Source prose uses a>0 while code uses n. No shared premise or diagram.

Full source pages 11 and 12 inspected to cover the stem, code and all choices. The positive-input recursive C function returns 1 at n=1, otherwise calls recursive(n-1) twice and adds their results. Ordinary nonmemoized call-tree cost gives T(n)=2T(n-1)+Theta(1). Source prose uses a>0 while code uses n. No shared premise or diagram.

Full page inspected, including four choices. T(n)=2T(n-1)+n*2^n for n>0, T(0)=1. Normalize by 2^n or unroll the unit-decrement recurrence and sum the weighted tolls. Unlike the 2004 constant-work call tree, the explicit toll adds a polynomial factor. No diagram/shared context.

groups.title: Infer a source category from observed evidence using Bayes
groups.subject: 12-discrete-mathematics
groups.rationale: Both supply a finite exhaustive partition with prior probabilities and conditional evidence likelihoods, then ask which partition category produced an observed outcome. Multiply each prior by its evidence likelihood, sum for the total evidence probability, and normalize the target category weight. The 2005 question has two bags with ball-count likelihoods; 2018 has three temperature states with a conditional-probability table. Other candidates ask total probability, unconditional events, conditional sample-space counts, or belong to another subject and are not included.

groups.title: Infer a binary source from an observed signal or outcome

In 2025 the source is a regular/fake coin; two tosses of the same coin first require computing the two-head likelihood. groups.title: Partition cache addresses into tag, set and offset
groups.subject: 02-computer-organization-architecture
groups.rationale: Convert capacity and block size into consistent addressable units, compute sets as capacity/(block size x ways), and partition address bits into offset, set index and tag. Variants ask a field width, set count, associativity, inverse memory/cache sizes, or a symbolic formula. Word-addressed questions must not use byte offsets; fully associative caches have zero index bits. The 2001 leaves retain their shared stem and distinct requested field. Exclude total metadata storage, concrete-address mapping and reference traces, page tables/TLBs, comparator-delay calculations and underdetermined maximum-cache-size searches. These are method variants, not identical statements or answers.

groups.title: Derive pipeline performance from weighted stall costs
groups.subject: 02-computer-organization-architecture
groups.rationale: Compute effective CPI as ideal throughput cost plus instruction-class frequency times stall cost, then combine CPI with clock period to obtain program time or a speedup ratio. 2006 derives a branch penalty and asks seconds; 2014 S1 has balanced stages and no clock overhead; 2014 S3 changes stage partitioning, clock rate and branch resolution depth; 2015 is the zero-stall special case; 2020 uses conditional cache-miss and branch rates; 2022 compares branch-prediction accuracy; 2024 and 2026 give aggregate stall fractions. Keep all frequency/latency assumptions and requested metrics explicit. Exclude finite per-instruction dependency schedules, fill/drain-only batches, and mere conceptual hazard statements.

sources.notes: Five stages at 1GHz; fetch first stage, conditional branch resolves third, fetching stops until known; 10^9 instructions, 20% branches, base one cycle each. Asks total program seconds; derive two-cycle branch penalty then weighted CPI. Full source/options inspected.

Asks old/new execution-time ratio with base CPI one for other instructions. Full source inspected; branch penalty and frequency both change.

Printed Q43: nonpipeline 2.5GHz and five CPI, pipeline 2GHz; instruction mix 30% memory, 60% ALU, remainder branch. Five percent of memory instructions stall fifty cycles, half of branches stall two, ALU none. Asks speedup; weighted stall rates must be conditional on instruction type. Full page inspected.
